messages:
alice: Heads-up — us-west GPU pools hit sustained saturation this morning, p99 token gen spiking to ~3.2s. Thinking we need a clearer playbook for queueing/admission: FIFO vs priority vs per-route. Any strong opinions? :warning:

ben: What metrics do we have? queue length, backlog seconds, drop counts?

alice: Quick snapshot from 08:12: 
```\nGPU util: 98% \navg queue length: 42 \nbacklog_seconds: 11.6 \np99 latency (served): 3.2s \nrejected_by_rate_limit: 0.6%\n```

carla: Per-route queues avoided head-of-line blocking for our multi-tenant test last month. Low overhead if we cap queue depth per route, but memory and scheduling complexity increase.

derek: Priority queues make sense for realtime customers, but we need admission control so higher priority doesn't starve background workloads. Token-bucket sized to capacity + dynamic refill based on free GPU slots?

elena: From product: SLA tiers require p99 < 1s for "realtime" customers. If we go priority, we need a guarantee path and a fallback path for overflow.

ben: Starvation is real — we've seen low-priority requests sit forever with strict priority. Recommend priority bands w/ aging (increase priority with wait time) as a start.

alice: Noted. We ran a FIFO trial in eu-west last week; reduced variance in served latency but tail for small tenants got horrible. TL;DR: pure FIFO -> decent avg, bad fairness.

carla: Implementation sketch: keep per-route token counters and a global slot estimate. Admission pseudocode: 
```\nif tokens[route] > 0 and global_slots > 0:
  allow()
else if queue_len(route) < max_per_route:
  enqueue(route)
else:
  reject_low_priority()
```
We can make tokens replenish proportional to recent utilization.

ops-bot: experiment-results/eu-west-fifo-2026-02-18.csv uploaded (63KB) :white_check_mark:

derek: Consider early-drop (RED/PIE style) for best-effort routes so they don't clog the queues. Also, probabilistic admission smooths bursts and prevents synchronized retries.

ben: Another lever: per-tenant soft quotas + burst buffer. If tenant bursts above quota, they get placed in a limited burst queue with lower weight. That keeps critical traffic flowing and is simpler than full priority tree.

alice: Cost tradeoff: adding dedicated headroom reduces utilization (more idle GPUs) but drops p99 dramatically. We should estimate cost per ms saved and align with SLA $ target.

elena: Can we document a hybrid proposal and a canary plan? Product needs to know how customers will be affected and what the intended rollback is.

carla: I'll draft a design: hybrid-per-route + priority bands + aging + RED for best-effort. Includes metrics to watch: p50/p95/p99 by tier, queue occupancy, GPU free-slots, enqueue/drop rates.

alice: Rollout checklist (quick):
- small canary in us-west with 10% traffic
- enable per-route queues + aging
- tune token refill to keep GPU slots ~20% free at peak
- watch p99 for realtime and tail for best-effort for 30m windows
- auto-disable if realtime p99 > baseline + 200ms

ben: Also add an alert for sustained queue growth > 60s backlog for > 5m.

derek: I'd add a short experiment to compare probabilistic drop thresholds (5%/10%/20%) to pick a sweet spot.

elena: Schedule a sync with sales/CS after canary so they can prep customer comms.

alice: OK I'll own the pilot, carla will do design doc, ben will own alerts, derek will run drop-threshold experiment. Meeting to follow in 20. :thumbsup:
